definition: A geneware modification package sold by Zheng-Dao Bioelectric that enhances peripheral nervous system response speed and pain modulation. Aggressively marketed to Tier 2-3 manual laborers as a productivity upgrade; critics note it also makes users easier to drive past safe working limits.
origin: Geneware trade name absorbed into common usage; the 'franchise' suffix comes from the subscription-based maintenance model
usage: Industrial workers, Ringo Heavy Industries laborers, combat personnel; also used disparagingly by labor advocates
example: Half the dock crew at the south terminal were running nerve franchise upgrades — they moved faster, complained less, and burned out in half the time.
